audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel chapter 23, first-pass restored draft
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Keilah food-system attack, repeated inquiry, followers' fear, battle and livestock, Abiathar's ephod, Saul's religious certainty, threatened siege, conditional oracle, six-hundred-person flight, Jonathan covenant, Ziphite informants, surveillance, near-encirclement, and Rock of Escape.

verses.restored: They told David, saying, Look, Philistines are fighting against Keilah and plundering threshing floors.

familiar.text: Then they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines fight against Keilah, and they rob the threshingfloors.

modern.text: Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֥דוּ לְדָוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֤ה פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ נִלְחָמִ֣ים בִּקְעִילָ֔ה וְהֵ֖מָּה שֹׁסִ֥ים אֶת הַגֳּרָנֽוֹת

verses.restored: David inquired of YHWH, saying, Shall I go and strike these Philistines? YHWH said to David, Go, strike Philistines, and save Keilah.

familiar.text: Therefore David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And the LORD said unto David, Go, and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah.

modern.text: So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?” And the LORD said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֵלֵ֣ךְ וְהִכֵּ֔יתִי בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל דָּוִ֗ד לֵ֚ךְ וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ֖ אֶת קְעִילָֽה

verses.restored: Men of David said to him, Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against ranks of Philistines?

familiar.text: And David’s men said unto him, Behold, we be afraid here in Judah: how much more then if we come to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?

modern.text: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י דָוִד֙ אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ פֹ֛ה בִּֽיהוּדָ֖ה יְרֵאִ֑ים וְאַף֙ כִּֽי נֵלֵ֣ךְ קְעִלָ֔ה אֶל מַֽעַרְכ֖וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: David again inquired of YHWH, and YHWH answered him and said, Arise, go down to Keilah, for I am giving Philistines into your hand.

familiar.text: Then David enquired of the LORD yet again. And the LORD answered him and said, Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into thine hand.

modern.text: Once again, David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him: “Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”

original.text: וַיּ֨וֹסֶף ע֤וֹד דָּוִד֙ לִשְׁאֹ֣ל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֖הוּ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר ק֚וּם רֵ֣ד קְעִילָ֔ה כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים בְּיָדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: David and his men went to Keilah, fought Philistines, drove away their livestock, and struck them with great blow. David saved inhabitants of Keilah.

familiar.text: So David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their cattle, and smote them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

modern.text: Then David and his men went to Keilah, fought against the Philistines, and carried off their livestock, striking them with a mighty blow. So David saved the people of Keilah.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִד֩ ואנשו קְעִילָ֜ה וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּנְהַג֙ אֶת מִקְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּ֥ךְ בָּהֶ֖ם מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣שַׁע דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֖ת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י קְעִילָֽה

verses.restored: When Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, an ephod had come down in his hand.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand.

modern.text: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod with him when he fled to David at Keilah.) Saul Pursues David (Psalms 54:1–7)

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּ֠בְרֹחַ אֶבְיָתָ֧ר בֶּן אֲחִימֶ֛לֶךְ אֶל דָּוִ֖ד קְעִילָ֑ה אֵפ֖וֹד יָרַ֥ד בְּיָדֽוֹ

verses.restored: It was told to Saul that David had come to Keilah. Saul said, Divine has alienated/closed him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a city of doors and bar.

familiar.text: And it was told Saul that David was come to Keilah. And Saul said, God hath delivered him into mine hand; for he is shut in, by entering into a town that hath gates and bars.

modern.text: When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars.”

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְשָׁא֔וּל כִּי בָ֥א דָוִ֖ד קְעִילָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל נִכַּ֨ר אֹת֤וֹ אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיָדִ֔י כִּ֚י נִסְגַּ֣ר לָב֔וֹא בְּעִ֖יר דְּלָתַ֥יִם וּבְרִֽיחַ

verses.restored: Saul summoned all people to war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.

familiar.text: And Saul called all the people together to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.

modern.text: Then Saul summoned all his troops to go to war at Keilah and besiege David and his men.

original.text: וַיְשַׁמַּ֥ע שָׁא֛וּל אֶת כָּל הָעָ֖ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה לָרֶ֣דֶת קְעִילָ֔ה לָצ֥וּר אֶל דָּוִ֖ד וְאֶל אֲנָשָֽׁיו

verses.restored: David knew Saul was devising harm against him, and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring near ephod.

familiar.text: And David knew that Saul secretly practised mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring hither the ephod.

modern.text: When David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod.”

original.text: וַיֵּ֣דַע דָּוִ֔ד כִּ֣י עָלָ֔יו שָׁא֖וּל מַחֲרִ֣ישׁ הָרָעָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל אֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן הַגִּ֖ישָׁה הָאֵפֽוֹד

verses.restored: David said, YHWH Divine of Israel, hearing, your servant has heard Saul seeks to come to Keilah to destroy city because of me.

familiar.text: Then said David, O LORD God of Israel, thy servant hath certainly heard that Saul seeketh to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.

modern.text: And David said, “O LORD, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city on my account.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ דָּוִד֒ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שָׁמֹ֤עַ שָׁמַע֙ עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּֽי מְבַקֵּ֥שׁ שָׁא֖וּל לָב֣וֹא אֶל קְעִילָ֑ה לְשַׁחֵ֥ת לָעִ֖יר בַּעֲבוּרִֽי

verses.restored: Will leaders of Keilah deliver me into his hand? Will Saul come down as your servant has heard? YHWH Divine of Israel, tell your servant, please. YHWH said, He will come down.

familiar.text: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as thy servant hath heard? O LORD God of Israel, I beseech thee, tell thy servant. And the LORD said, He will come down.

modern.text: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD, God of Israel, please tell Your servant.” “He will,” said the LORD.

original.text: הֲיַסְגִּרֻ֣נִי בַעֲלֵי֩ קְעִילָ֨ה בְיָד֜וֹ הֲיֵרֵ֣ד שָׁא֗וּל כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁמַ֣ע עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַגֶּד נָ֖א לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרֵֽד

verses.restored: David said, Will leaders of Keilah deliver me and my men into hand of Saul? YHWH said, They will deliver.

familiar.text: Then said David, Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul? And the LORD said, They will deliver thee up.

modern.text: So David asked, “Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?” “They will,” said the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד הֲיַסְגִּ֜רוּ בַּעֲלֵ֧י קְעִילָ֛ה אֹתִ֥י וְאֶת אֲנָשַׁ֖י בְּיַד שָׁא֑וּל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יַסְגִּֽירוּ

verses.restored: David arose with his men, about six hundred, and they went out from Keilah and moved wherever they could. It was told to Saul David escaped from Keilah, and he ceased going out.

familiar.text: Then David and his men, which were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go. And it was told Saul that David was escaped from Keilah; and he forbare to go forth.

modern.text: Then David and his men, about six hundred strong, set out and departed from Keilah, moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he declined to go forth.

original.text: וַיָּקָם֩ דָּוִ֨ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו כְּשֵׁשׁ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ וַיֵּצְאוּ֙ מִקְּעִלָ֔ה וַיִּֽתְהַלְּכ֖וּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְהַלָּ֑כוּ וּלְשָׁא֣וּל הֻגַּ֗ד כִּֽי נִמְלַ֤ט דָּוִד֙ מִקְּעִילָ֔ה וַיֶּחְדַּ֖ל לָצֵֽאת

verses.restored: David stayed in wilderness in strongholds and stayed in hill country in wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him all days, but Divine did not give him into his hand.

familiar.text: And David abode in the wilderness in strong holds, and remained in a mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand.

modern.text: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב דָּוִ֤ד בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ בַּמְּצָד֔וֹת וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בָּהָ֖ר בְּמִדְבַּר זִ֑יף וַיְבַקְשֵׁ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ כָּל הַיָּמִ֔ים וְלֹֽא נְתָנ֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדֽוֹ

verses.restored: David saw Saul had gone out to seek his life. David was in wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.

familiar.text: And David saw that Saul was come out to seek his life: and David was in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood.

modern.text: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא דָוִ֔ד כִּֽי יָצָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל לְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְדָוִ֥ד בְּמִדְבַּר זִ֖יף בַּחֹֽרְשָׁה

verses.restored: Jonathan son of Saul arose and went to David at Horesh and strengthened his hand in Divine.

familiar.text: And Jonathan Saul’s son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God.

modern.text: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,

original.text: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בֶּן שָׁא֔וּל וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אֶל דָּוִ֖ד חֹ֑רְשָׁה וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק אֶת יָד֖וֹ בֵּאלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: He said to him, Do not fear, for hand of Saul my father shall not find you. You will reign over Israel, and I shall be second to you. Saul my father also knows this.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee; and that also Saul my father knoweth.

modern.text: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו אַל תִּירָ֗א כִּ֠י לֹ֤א תִֽמְצָאֲךָ֙ יַ֚ד שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֔י וְאַתָּה֙ תִּמְלֹ֣ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָנֹכִ֖י אֶֽהְיֶה לְּךָ֣ לְמִשְׁנֶ֑ה וְגַם שָׁא֥וּל אָבִ֖י יֹדֵ֥עַ כֵּֽן

verses.restored: The two cut covenant before YHWH. David stayed at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.

familiar.text: And they two made a covenant before the LORD: and David abode in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house.

modern.text: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.

original.text: וַיִּכְרְת֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם בְּרִ֖ית לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב דָּוִד֙ בַּחֹ֔רְשָׁה וִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן הָלַ֥ךְ לְבֵיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, Is not David hiding with us in strongholds at Horesh, on hill of Hachilah south of Jeshimon?

familiar.text: Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon?

modern.text: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah south of Jeshimon?

original.text: וַיַּעֲל֤וּ זִפִים֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל הַגִּבְעָ֖תָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲל֣וֹא דָ֠וִד מִסְתַּתֵּ֨ר עִמָּ֤נוּ בַמְּצָדוֹת֙ בַּחֹ֔רְשָׁה בְּגִבְעַת֙ הַֽחֲכִילָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִימִ֥ין הַיְשִׁימֽוֹן

verses.restored: Now according to all desire of your life, king, come down; ours is to deliver him into hand of king.

familiar.text: Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of thy soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand.

modern.text: Now, O king, come down whenever your soul desires, and we will be responsible for delivering him into your hand.”

original.text: וְ֠עַתָּה לְכָל אַוַּ֨ת נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לָרֶ֖דֶת רֵ֑ד וְלָ֥נוּ הַסְגִּיר֖וֹ בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Saul said, Blessed are you of YHWH, because you have had compassion on me.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Blessed be ye of the LORD; for ye have compassion on me.

modern.text: “May you be blessed by the LORD,” replied Saul, “for you have had compassion on me.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל בְּרוּכִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י חֲמַלְתֶּ֖ם עָלָֽי

verses.restored: Go, please, make yet more certain. Know and see his place, where his foot is, who has seen him there, for it is said to me he is very cunning.

familiar.text: Go, I pray you, prepare yet, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who hath seen him there: for it is told me that he dealeth very subtilly.

modern.text: Please go and prepare further. Investigate and watch carefully where he goes and who has seen him there, for I am told that he is extremely cunning.

original.text: לְכוּ נָ֞א הָכִ֣ינוּ ע֗וֹד וּדְע֤וּ וּרְאוּ֙ אֶת מְקוֹמוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה רַגְל֔וֹ מִ֥י רָאָ֖הוּ שָׁ֑ם כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עָר֥וֹם יַעְרִ֖ם הֽוּא

verses.restored: See and know all hiding places where he hides. Return to me with certainty, and I will go with you. If he is in land, I will search him among all thousands/clans of Judah.

familiar.text: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hideth himself, and come ye again to me with the certainty, and I will go with you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I will search him out throughout all the thousands of Judah.

modern.text: Observe and find out all the places where he hides. Then come back to me with certainty, and I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will search him out among all the clans of Judah.”

original.text: וּרְא֣וּ וּדְע֗וּ מִכֹּ֤ל הַמַּֽחֲבֹאִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְחַבֵּ֣א שָׁ֔ם וְשַׁבְתֶּ֤ם אֵלַי֙ אֶל נָכ֔וֹן וְהָלַכְתִּ֖י אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְהָיָה֙ אִם יֶשְׁנ֣וֹ בָאָ֔רֶץ וְחִפַּשְׂתִּ֣י אֹת֔וֹ בְּכֹ֖ל אַלְפֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: They arose and went to Ziph before Saul. David and his men were in wilderness of Maon, in Arabah south of Jeshimon.

familiar.text: And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon.

modern.text: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon in the Arabah south of Jeshimon,

original.text: וַיָּק֛וּמוּ וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ זִ֖יפָה לִפְנֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וְדָוִ֨ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו בְּמִדְבַּ֤ר מָעוֹן֙ בָּעֲרָבָ֔ה אֶ֖ל יְמִ֥ין הַיְשִׁימֽוֹן

verses.restored: Saul and his men went to seek, and it was told to David. He went down to rock and stayed in wilderness of Maon. Saul heard and pursued David in wilderness of Maon.

familiar.text: Saul also and his men went to seek him. And they told David: wherefore he came down into a rock, and abode in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.

modern.text: and Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard of this, he pursued David there.

verses.restored: Saul went on one side of mountain, and David and his men on other side. David was hurrying to go away from before Saul, while Saul and his men were surrounding David and his men to seize them.

familiar.text: And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them.

modern.text: Saul was proceeding along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side. Even though David was hurrying to get away, Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them.

verses.restored: A messenger came to Saul, saying, Hurry and come, for Philistines have made a raid upon land.

familiar.text: But there came a messenger unto Saul, saying, Haste thee, and come; for the Philistines have invaded the land.

modern.text: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Come quickly, for the Philistines have raided the land!”

verses.restored: Saul returned from pursuing David and went to meet Philistines. Therefore they called that place Rock of Divisions/Escape.

familiar.text: Wherefore Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Selahammahlekoth.

modern.text: So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why that place is called Sela-hammahlekoth.

verses.restored: David went up from there and stayed in strongholds of En-gedi.

modern.text: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En-gedi.

translation_notes: Keilah faces economic attack at threshing floors. Food systems and civilians are central to the crisis, not merely military territory.
David's men openly name fear. A leader's repeated discernment should include the fear, consent, and capacity of vulnerable followers rather than shame them.
The rescue includes battlefield killing and seizure of livestock. Saving a city does not make all wartime actions beyond moral examination.
Saul interprets David's location as Divine delivery while planning siege and city destruction. Religious certainty can be profoundly wrong when joined to coercive power.
The oracle about Keilah's leaders describes a likely future under pressure, not a moral license to condemn the whole city as traitorous.
David leaves rather than make Keilah absorb a siege on his behalf. Refugee movements may protect both fugitives and host communities.
Jonathan strengthens David and acknowledges a future he believes will displace his own dynasty. Their covenant remains intimate and political.
The Ziphites' cooperation with Saul may reflect local fear, politics, or survival; the text does not justify hatred of a population or place.
Saul blesses informants in YHWH's name while hunting David. Divine language does not validate surveillance, informant systems, or persecution.
The near-encirclement and sudden Philistine raid show contingency rather than a simple triumphal rescue formula.
Names such as Rock of Escape preserve survival memory; they do not prove that all later political claims attached to a place are Divinely guaranteed.
safety_note: Do not shame David's men for fear, condemn all Keilahites or Ziphites as betrayers, or use Divine guidance language to justify surveillance, siege, informant networks, or political pursuit. Saul sincerely invokes YHWH while planning harm, demonstrating that religious certainty is not moral proof. Refugees may leave a host community to prevent collective punishment, and communities under pressure should not be judged as though they possess unlimited freedom.
